title: Where do video editors get their clips and how to manage them on Mac
metaTitle: Where do video editors get their clips: Asset sourcing fixes for Mac
description: Video editors get their clips from local drives, NAS, and cloud storage, but sourcing is a bottleneck. Learn how to manage assets efficiently on your Mac.
targetKeyword: where do video editors get their clips
intro: Video editors get their clips from a mix of local SSDs, network attached storage, and cloud repositories. This sourcing process often becomes a major bottleneck, consuming 30 to 90 minutes of prep time before an editor makes a single cut.
tldr: Asset sourcing is the hidden cost that eats up to 90 minutes of your day.
Fragmented storage and poor metadata are the primary causes of search friction.
You can fix your workflow with better indexing and centralized storage without buying expensive enterprise software.
Lazur helps you find and organize your files by answering questions about your screen content.

blocks.text: Why finding clips takes so long

When you ask where do video editors get their clips, the answer is everywhere. Footage lives on SD cards, external NVMe drives, NAS arrays, and cloud sync folders. This fragmentation is the root of digital chaos. Because files often have names like DSC_4827.MOV, you cannot find them with a simple search. You must manually scrub through hours of footage to find the right take. This manual labor turns creative professionals into file clerks.
The hidden costs of poor asset management

Inefficient sourcing creates a budget bleed. Every minute spent searching for a missing B-roll clip is a minute you cannot bill for actual editing. In manual workflows, batch-processing just 3 to 5 clips can take 8 to 12 hours of total time. This includes importing, transcoding, and tagging. When projects scale, the risk of duplication and version control errors increases. You might end up working on the wrong version of a project file, leading to costly revision cycles that delay delivery.
How to fix your asset sourcing workflow

items: Create a single source of truth by centralizing all project assets in one folder structure.
Use AI-powered indexing tools to search by content, such as faces or objects, instead of filenames.
Generate proxies early to keep your timeline fast and your storage requirements manageable.
Establish a consistent metadata standard for every file you ingest into your project.

blocks.text: Mac apps to help with file management

You do not need to buy an expensive enterprise asset management system to see improvements. Adobe Bridge is a free tool that connects directly to Premiere Pro and After Effects. For DaVinci Resolve users, the built-in Media Pool includes AI IntelliSearch as of version 21. For general file management, Commander One offers dual-pane transfers that make moving files between drives faster. If you struggle with duplicates, Gemini can help you clear out redundant files that clutter your drives.
How Lazur helps you find and organize assets

Lazur helps you bridge the gap between your files and your editing software. Because Lazur sees your screen, you can ask it where a specific folder is or how to perform a complex task in your editor. If you are lost in a deep Finder directory, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur to point to the folder you need. It circles the item on your screen. This saves you from clicking through nested folders repeatedly.

faq.question: Where do video editors get their clips?
faq.answer: Editors source clips from local external drives, network storage, and cloud services. The challenge is not the source, but the organization.

faq.question: Is there a free way to organize video assets?
faq.answer: Yes. Adobe Bridge is a free asset browser that works well with Adobe tools. DaVinci Resolve also has built-in AI search features.

faq.question: How can I stop wasting time searching for files?
faq.answer: Implement a strict folder naming convention, use AI-based indexing tools, and clear out duplicate files regularly.

causes.title: Fragmented storage
causes.text: Footage is often split between SD cards, local SSDs, and network storage, making it impossible to search everything at once.

causes.title: Meaningless metadata
causes.text: Camera-generated filenames like DSC_4827.MOV provide no context, forcing manual inspection of every clip.

fixes.title: Centralize your assets
fixes.text: Move all files for a single project into one master folder structure before you start editing.
